company.name: Ironleaf Manufacturing
company.summary: Ironleaf Manufacturing is a custom metal parts maker in Ohio with about 160 employees. You run CNC machining and sheet metal work for industrial buyers who send drawings and RFQs by email. Your team covers production, quality, purchasing, sales engineering, planning and finance, with Epicor as the main ERP.
offerings: CNC machining of custom metal parts
Sheet metal fabrication, including cutting, forming and welding
Custom quoting from drawings and CAD files
Low to medium volume production runs
Quality inspection and first article documentation
Finishing and light assembly for metal components
company.customers: Industrial OEMs, machine builders and product companies in North America. Your buyers are design engineers, purchasing managers and supply chain teams who send drawings and RFQs by email.
tech_signals: CAD/CAM software for CNC and sheet metal
Calipers, micrometers and CMM for inspection

roles.title: CNC Machinist
repetitive_tasks: Load programs and set up machines
Check parts with calipers and micrometers

roles.title: Welder and Fabricator
repetitive_tasks: Set up fixtures and weld parts

strategy.situation: Ironleaf Manufacturing runs custom CNC and sheet metal work for industrial buyers who send drawings and RFQs by email. Epicor, CAD/CAM and spreadsheets hold the core data, but much of the daily coordination still moves through email and manual entry.
strategy.complication: As order volume and customer expectations rise, your skilled estimators, quality engineers and planners spend hours copying data and chasing status instead of solving manufacturing problems. Delays in quotes, quality packets and promise dates put repeat business at risk.
strategy.governing_thought: Start with an RFQ intake and quote drafting agent, a first article and PPAP packet agent, and a planner expedite and status update agent to cut response delays and free skilled time.

key_arguments.headline: Repetitive work concentrates in RFQ triage, quality packets and planning firefighting
key_arguments.support: Your sales engineers read drawings, build estimates and chase updates by hand. Quality engineers copy inspection results into FAI and PPAP forms while planners and expediters rebuild status reports from Epicor and email.

key_arguments.headline: These three agents use email, Epicor reports and existing templates
key_arguments.support: These three workflows repeat every day, touch many orders and use data you already have in Epicor, email and shared drives. They need human review, so they build trust without touching machine controls or final pricing.

key_arguments.headline: Run supervised pilots with named owners, then expand after two clean weeks
key_arguments.support: Give each agent a named owner, run it in draft mode and review samples daily for two weeks before it sends anything. After that, expand to more order types and add the next agents in purchasing, finance and maintenance.

strategy.executive_summary: Ironleaf Manufacturing runs custom CNC and sheet metal work for industrial buyers who send drawings and RFQs by email. Epicor, CAD/CAM and spreadsheets hold the core data, but much of the daily coordination still moves through email and manual entry. As order volume and customer expectations rise, your skilled estimators, quality engineers and planners spend hours copying data and chasing status instead of solving manufacturing problems. Delays in quotes, quality packets and promise dates put repeat business at risk. Start with an RFQ intake and quote drafting agent, a first article and PPAP packet agent, and a planner expedite and status update agent to cut response delays and free skilled time.

maturity.label: Early
maturity.note: You have strong ERP and CAD systems but little automation between email, Epicor and documents. First wins should avoid machine controls and focus on office workflows.

opportunities.title: RFQ emails become draft quotes in hours
opportunities.description: The agent reads incoming RFQ emails and attachments, extracts part specs, checks Epicor history and drafts a cost estimate with a customer reply. Your estimator reviews, adjusts and approves before anything goes out.
before: CSR opens RFQ email and saves drawings to a folder
Estimator reads prints and marks material and operations
Estimator checks similar jobs in Epicor and spreadsheets
Estimator builds quote in Excel and writes reply
Estimator emails quote and logs it in CRM
after: Agent captures the email and attachments
Agent extracts key specs and pulls similar job history
Agent drafts the estimate and customer reply
Human: estimator reviews, adjusts pricing and approves
Human: estimator sends the quote and agent logs it

opportunities.title: First article and PPAP packets assembled automatically
opportunities.description: The agent collects inspection results, drawing revisions and material certs into a draft FAI or PPAP packet. It flags missing data so your quality engineer only reviews and signs.
before: Inspector runs checks and logs results
Quality engineer gathers drawing and revision data
Quality engineer copies certs and results into forms
Quality engineer checks packet against customer checklist
Quality manager signs and sends packet
after: Agent pulls inspection results from CMM and shared drive
Agent gathers certs, revisions and customer checklist
Agent drafts FAI or PPAP packet and flags gaps
Human: quality engineer reviews and corrects
Human: quality manager signs and sends

opportunities.title: Planner sends daily hot list and promise date alerts
opportunities.description: The agent checks Epicor work orders and material status, then drafts a hot list and promise date changes for sales and the shop. Your planner approves exceptions and the expediter handles floor issues.

Planner checks Epicor work orders and material
Scheduler updates hot list in Excel
Planner emails sales about date changes
Expediter calls floor leads to move priority jobs
after: Agent pulls work order and material status from Epicor
Agent ranks at-risk jobs and drafts hot list
Agent drafts promise date alerts to sales
Human: planner approves exceptions and date changes
Human: expediter handles floor moves and supplier calls

opportunities.title: Supplier PO follow-ups sent before material runs late
opportunities.description: The agent monitors open purchase orders in Epicor and sends polite follow-up requests when promised dates pass. It also matches packing lists to receipts and flags short shipments.

Buyer emails suppliers for status
Buyer updates lead times in Epicor
Receiving clerk counts material and matches packing list
Clerk enters receipt and tells buyer about shortages
after: Agent reviews open POs and promised dates
Agent drafts supplier follow-up emails
Human: buyer approves follow-ups and handles exceptions
Agent matches packing lists to receipts
Human: receiving clerk counts and confirms receipt

opportunities.title: Calibration reminders and logs kept current
opportunities.description: The agent tracks gauge calibration dates, drafts reminders and updates the calibration log when records are filed. Your technician handles physical checks and outside scheduling.

Technician emails reminders to tool owners
Technician schedules outside calibration
Technician files certificates in shared drive
Manager reviews overdue gauges
after: Agent checks calibration dates and drafts reminders
Agent flags overdue gauges to technician
Human: technician checks gauge condition
Human: technician schedules outside calibration
Agent files records and updates log after human confirms

opportunities.title: AP invoice matching reviewed before month end
opportunities.description: The agent matches incoming AP invoices to Epicor purchase orders and receiving records, then drafts exceptions for review. Your accountant approves matches and posts only the exceptions.

Accountant finds matching PO in Epicor
Accountant checks receiving record
Accountant enters invoice or marks exception
Controller reviews month end accruals
after: Agent reads invoice PDFs and pulls PO and receipt data
Agent matches invoices and flags price or quantity gaps
Agent drafts entry or exception note
Human: accountant reviews and approves matches
Human: controller reviews exceptions and close items

opportunities.title: Maintenance PMs and spare parts checked daily
opportunities.description: The agent reviews the PM schedule, checks spare parts in Epicor and drafts work orders for due maintenance. Your technicians complete the work and log repairs.

Manager checks spare parts stock
Manager writes work orders for due PMs
Technician completes PM and logs repairs
Manager reviews downtime report

Agent flags parts shortages to manager

Human: manager reviews downtime and approves follow-up

opportunities.title: Shift handoff notes written from daily logs
opportunities.description: The agent summarizes production counts, open issues and machine notes into a draft shift handoff. Supervisors review the draft and add floor context.

Operators tell supervisor about issues
Supervisor writes handoff email
Supervisor calls next shift lead
Next shift starts with incomplete notes
after: Agent pulls production counts and open work orders
Agent drafts shift handoff summary

Human: supervisor sends handoff to next shift
Agent logs acknowledged issues

opportunities.title: Customer order status replies drafted from Epicor
opportunities.description: The agent reads status request emails, checks Epicor order and work order status, and drafts a reply with current promise dates. Your CSR reviews and sends, or escalates exceptions.
before: CSR opens customer status email
CSR looks up order in Epicor
CSR checks work order and shipping status
CSR writes reply or asks planner
CSR logs note in CRM
after: Agent reads status request and pulls Epicor order data
Agent drafts reply with current promise date
Agent flags jobs needing planner or account manager input
Human: CSR reviews and sends reply
Human: account manager handles exceptions

roadmap.title: Prove three office agents with supervised daily review
items: Set up RFQ intake and quote draft agent for one sales engineer team
Set up FAI and PPAP packet agent for one quality engineer
Set up planner hot list and promise date agent for one planner and expediter
Review samples daily, fix exceptions and record hours saved
Hold a 30-minute weekly check with each named owner

roadmap.title: Add purchasing, finance and maintenance agents after phase 1 signs off
items: Add supplier PO follow-up and receipt matching agent
Add AP invoice matching agent for one accountant
Add maintenance PM and spare parts agent for one maintenance manager
Add calibration log agent for one quality technician
Expand phase 1 agents to more order types and users

roadmap.title: Scale to more workflows and users as your team takes ownership
items: Add shift handoff and customer status reply agents
Train internal owners to adjust prompts, templates and exception rules
Review KPI trends monthly and retire any agent that does not save time
Add new agents only after existing agents meet review and accuracy targets

risks.risk: Bad data in Epicor or drawings leads to wrong drafts
risks.mitigation: Keep human approval on all customer-facing and financial outputs, run daily sample audits and correct data at the source.

risks.risk: Estimators or quality staff do not trust agent output
risks.mitigation: Name one owner per agent, start in draft mode, and let the owner set the review rules before anything is sent.

risks.risk: Email and attachment access raises security concerns
risks.mitigation: Limit each agent to a shared mailbox and specific folders, use least-privilege access and log every action.

risks.risk: Scope creep across too many workflows slows the first wins
risks.mitigation: Freeze the phase 1 list until each agent meets its accuracy and time-saving targets, then add the next agents.

risks.risk: Customer-specific quote or PPAP formats vary too much
risks.mitigation: Build a template library for the top formats and route unusual requests to a human exception queue.

kpis: Quote turnaround time from RFQ email to sent quote
FAI and PPAP packet cycle time
AP invoice match rate without manual touch
Hours saved per week by agent, validated by supervisors
User adoption rate for phase 1 agents
